observation.visible_scene: A macro/microscopic view on a pale, near-white background: a large dark circular liquid mass sits center-right, ringed by chains of smaller dark droplets arranged in curved arcs (an upper arc, a left-pointing branching tail ending in a larger dot, a lower arc, and a short vertical column on the right). A small 'CHEMICAL BOUILLON' logo is fixed at the bottom-right corner throughout.
visible_changes: For the first portion of the clip (frames 1–22) the droplet pattern and the large mass are essentially static, with only negligible drift.
Around frame 23 a blurred dark elongated rod/stick enters from the right edge and moves diagonally toward the center, coming to hover over the right side of the large mass.
From frame 25 to the end the rod translates slowly leftward/across the top of the large mass, partially occluding it; the mass's outline stays roughly the same size while the rod covers part of it.

The right-side vertical column of small droplets and the upper arc appear to shift slightly leftward/closer to the main mass over the course of the clip, while the left tail and lower arc remain in broadly similar positions.
The fixed logo position suggests the camera is stationary, so the observed shifts are object motion rather than camera pan.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the rod (magnet, probe, needle) and the reason it approaches are not shown.
The cause of the initial droplet arrangement and the nature of the dark liquid are not visible.
What happens after the rod's motion in the last frame is outside the segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the large mass's left-edge outline genuinely deforms or the apparent notch is occlusion/noise is unclear.
Exact per-droplet displacements are small and hard to separate from slight focus/positioning changes.
The rod's depth relative to the mass (touching vs hovering above) cannot be confirmed from these frames.
